h: Timings, wildlife and the road through the hills
p: The reserve sits beside the A708, roughly ten miles north-east of Moffat on the scenic road towards Selkirk. That drive is a treat in itself, winding through steep-sided valleys with hardly a building in sight. Give yourself extra time and enjoy it.

How long you need depends on your plans. A look at the falls from the lower path might take half an hour or so. The climb up to Loch Skeen and back is a different matter, usually a few hours with breaks, and it's steep in places with drops beside the path. Keep children close and dogs on leads on the higher sections, and don't go off-path for a better view of the falls.
Wildlife fans should look out for the reserve's feral goats, which are a regular sight on the slopes, and peregrine falcons, which have nested in the area. Bring binoculars and a bit of patience.

Mobile signal is unreliable here, so download any maps before you leave Moffat and tell someone your plans if you're heading up to the loch. Pack a flask and some food too, as there's nothing to buy up the glen.

Carry on along the A708 and you'll reach St Mary's Loch, a beautiful stretch of water with walks along its shore. Back in Moffat, the famous ram statue stands proudly in the High Street, and Moffat Toffee is a sweet way to round off the trip. North of the town, the Devil's Beef Tub is a dramatic hollow in the hills with a dark history of cattle raiders.
